events.title: King John Seals the Magna Carta
events.description: At Runnymede near Windsor, England, King John affixed his seal to the Magna Carta under pressure from rebellious barons. The charter limited royal authority and asserted that the king was subject to the law.
events.significance: The Magna Carta became a foundational document for constitutional government and the rule of law, influencing later legal and democratic traditions including the U.S. Constitution.

events.title: Benjamin Franklin's Kite Experiment
events.description: According to traditional accounts, Benjamin Franklin flew a kite during a thunderstorm in Philadelphia to demonstrate that lightning is electrical in nature. The date is commonly cited, though historians debate the details of the experiment.
events.significance: The experiment advanced understanding of electricity and led to the invention of the lightning rod, which protected buildings from fire and damage.

events.title: Arkansas Admitted as the 25th U.S. State
events.description: Arkansas became the 25th state of the United States, entering the Union as a slave state shortly before Michigan was admitted as a free state, preserving the balance in the Senate.
events.significance: Its admission reflected the sectional tensions over slavery that shaped U.S. politics before the Civil War, and it expanded American statehood west of the Mississippi River.

events.title: Battle of Saipan Begins
events.description: U.S. forces landed on Saipan in the Mariana Islands during World War II, beginning a major amphibious campaign against Japanese defenders.
events.significance: The capture of Saipan put U.S. bombers within range of the Japanese home islands and contributed to the collapse of Japan's inner defensive perimeter in the Pacific.

events.title: IRA Bombing in Manchester
events.description: The Provisional IRA detonated a large truck bomb in central Manchester, England, injuring over 200 people and causing extensive damage to the city center, though there were no fatalities.
events.significance: It was one of the largest bombs detonated in Britain since World War II and led to major urban redevelopment in Manchester, while underscoring the urgency of the peace process in Northern Ireland.
